description: The portfolio's configuration, extended by name rather than copied: the Monday batch, the labels, the kotlin / kotlinx / sborka / ci-actions groups and the stack held until Kotlin 2.5.20 (Kotlin 2.4, KSP 2.3, Compose 1.12, Gradle 9.8) live in `github>youndie/sborka`. It replaces Renovate's onboarding `config:recommended`, which would have offered Compose 1.13 and the Gradle after 9.8 that the rest of the portfolio holds back.

`automerge-harness` is extended second, with one exception written below. The reason this file used to give for leaving it out still holds and is now what the exception is for: `stand.yaml` — the one that publishes the stand's images — runs only on a `v*` tag, and `docker/login-action` is used there and by no pull request, so a harness major of it would merge itself green and fail at the next release. That action waits for a person; every other action and the Gradle wrapper are exercised by `check.yaml` on every `pull_request` (the docs gate, gradle, the image, the chart and the e2e) and merge themselves on green. Re-checked 2026-11-25.
Nothing repository-specific is added: the images the chart names (PostgreSQL, shildik, the bootstrap's Python) are offered like any other dependency and read by a person.

The actions that only `stand.yaml` uses wait for a person: that workflow runs on a tag (or by hand), no pull request runs it, so a green pull request says nothing about them and a broken one would surface at the next release, not on the merge. Every other action and the wrapper merge themselves through `automerge-harness`, because the pull-request workflows ran exactly those versions.

AFTER the presets, because the last match wins, and in a group of its own: Renovate merges a grouped pull request only when every update in it may merge, so left in `ci actions` these would hold every other action with them. The list is what that workflow uses and no pull-request workflow does (re-checked 2026-11-25); an action added to that workflow later is not on it until somebody adds it here.
